nodes.name: Proof that cube root of 2 is irrational
nodes.statement: The following theorem will be used without proof, as it is already available in MathLib: \begin{theorem*} For any $x\in(\R\setminus\Z)$ if there exist an $n\in \N_{>0}$ and $m\in\Z$ such that $m = x^n$, then $x$ is rational. \end{theorem*} The fact that $(\sqrt[3]{2})^3=2$, allows us to deduce that the only remaining task is to prove that it is not an integer. This can be observed trough two relations. \begin{align} 2^{\frac{1}{3}} &< 2 \\ 2^{\frac{1}{3}} &> 1 \end{align}

nodes.name: Proof that X^3-2 is irreducible
nodes.statement: Since $\mathbb{Q}$ is $a$ subfield of $\mathbb{C} [X]$, we know that \begin{equation*} X^3 - 2 = (X - \sqrt[3]{2})(X -\zeta_3 \sqrt[3]{2})(X -\zeta_3^2 \sqrt[3]{2}) \end{equation*} Suppose $P$ is reducible, then \begin{equation*} X^3 - 2 = (X - a)(X^2 + bX + c)\text{, with } a, b, c \in \mathbb{Q} \end{equation*} In particular it has a zero in $\mathbb{Q}$, so there is a rational number $a$ such that $a^3 = 2$.\newline But we know that $\zeta_3 \sqrt[3]{2}$ and $\zeta_3^2 \sqrt[3]{2}$ are not real numbers and $\sqrt[3]{2}$ is not rational \ref{lem:irrational_thirdroot_two}. So $P$ is irreducible over $\mathbb{Q}$.
nodes.statement_short: A reducible cubic has a rational root, but the roots of $X^3-2$ are non-real or irrational.

nodes.name: Proof that the cube cannot be doubled
nodes.statement: By applying the corollary \ref{cor:Classfication_z_in_M_inf_2m_not}, it is sufficient to proof that no $m\in \N$ exists such that $$2^m\overset{?}{=}[\sqrt[3]{2}:\Q({0,1})]\overset{0,1\in\Q}{=} [\sqrt[3]{2}:\Q] = \text{degree}(\mu_{\Q,\sqrt[3]{2}}).$$ Since $P$ is irreducible over $\mathbb{Q}$ \ref{thm:irreducible_over_Q}, monic and has $\sqrt[3]{2}$ as a zero, we know that $[\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt[3]{2}):\mathbb{Q}] = 3$. And since $$ 3 \equiv_2 1 \neq 0 \equiv_2 = 2^m \qquad\forall m \in \N$$ we can conclude that the cube can't be doubled using a compass and straightedge.
nodes.statement_short: $[\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt[3]2):\mathbb{Q}]=3$ is not a power of 2, so the non-constructibility criterion applies.

nodes.name: Trisection of an angle
nodes.statement: The trisection of an angle with a compass and ruler can be reduced to the following problem:\\ Let $\mathcal{M} = \{a, b, c\}$ with $a, b, c$ not on a line and $\alpha := \angle (b - a, c - a)$ be the resulting angle. Then $\alpha$ can be trisected if and only if there is a point $d\in \mathcal{M}_{\infty}$ such that $\angle (b - a, d - a) = \alpha/3$.
nodes.statement_short: Trisecting the angle at $a$ between $b$ and $c$ means constructing $d$ with angle $\alpha/3$ from $\{a,b,c\}$.

nodes.name: Angle trisection problem
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{M} = \{0,1,\exp(\textbf{i} \alpha)\}$. $$\text{Is }\exp(\textbf{i} \alpha/3) \overset{?}{\in} \mathcal{M}_{\infty}?$$
nodes.statement_short: Is $e^{\imath\alpha/3}$ constructible from $\{0,1,e^{\imath\alpha}\}$?

nodes.name: K_0 for trisection
nodes.statement: In this context, since the numbers zero and one are rational numbers, it can be concluded that $K_0$ is equal to $$ K_0 = \mathbb{Q}(\mathcal{M}\cup Conj(\mathcal{M})) = \mathbb{Q}(e^{\imath\alpha},\overline{e^{\imath\alpha}}). $$
nodes.statement_short: For $\mathcal{M}=\{0,1,e^{\imath\alpha}\}$, $K_0=\mathbb{Q}(e^{\imath\alpha},\overline{e^{\imath\alpha}})$.
assumptions: the numbers zero and one are rational numbers

nodes.name: Equivalent forms of non-trisectability
nodes.statement: Given the corollary reference and the fact that $e^{\imath\alpha/3}$ is a zero of $X^3 - e^{\imath\alpha}\in \mathbb{Q}(e^{\imath\alpha},\overline{e^{\imath\alpha}})[X]$, the following is equivalent: \begin{itemize} \item $\exp(\textbf{i} \alpha/3) \notin \mathcal{M}_{\infty}$ \item $\text{degree}(\mu_{e^{\imath\alpha/3},K_0}) = 3$ \item $X^3 - e^{\imath\alpha}$ is irreducible over $\mathbb{Q}(e^{\imath\alpha},\overline{e^{\imath\alpha}})$ \end{itemize}
nodes.statement_short: $e^{\imath\alpha/3}$ is not constructible iff its minimal polynomial over $K_0$ has degree 3 iff $X^3-e^{\imath\alpha}$ is irreducible.

nodes.name: Degree of K_0 for 60 degrees
nodes.statement: The degree of $K_0 = \mathbb{Q}(e^{\imath\frac{\pi}{3}},\overline{e^{\imath\frac{\pi}{3}}})$ is equal to $2$.
conclusions: The degree of $K_0 = \mathbb{Q}(e^{\imath\frac{\pi}{3}},\overline{e^{\imath\frac{\pi}{3}}})$ is equal to $2$.
nodes.label: lem:degree_K0_angel

nodes.name: Proof of degree of K_0 for 60 degrees
nodes.statement: For all real numbers $\alpha$, we have that $$ \exp(\imath \alpha) = \cos(\alpha) + \imath \sin(\alpha).$$ For $\alpha = \pi / 3$ we get \begin{equation*} \cos(\alpha) = \frac{1}{2}\qquad \text{and}\qquad \sin(\alpha) = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \end{equation*} Therefore $\mathbb{Q}(e^{\imath\frac{\pi}{3}},\overline{e^{\imath\frac{\pi}{3}}})$ is in $\mathbb{Q}(\imath\sqrt{3})$. And since $\imath\sqrt{3}$ is a zero of $X^2 + 3$, we know that the degree of $K_0$ less then $2$. To show that the degree is not $1$, we apply the fact that $\imath\sqrt{3} \notin \mathbb{Q}$.
nodes.statement_short: $K_0=\mathbb{Q}(\imath\sqrt3)$, a root of $X^2+3$ not in $\mathbb{Q}$.

nodes.name: Proof that 60 degrees cannot be trisected
nodes.statement: By utilising the aforementioned lemma \ref{lem:degree_K0_angel} to apply the corresponding corollary \ref{cor:Classfication_z_in_M_inf_2m_rat}, we can narrow our focus to the degree over $\Q$. Now we use the fact that if $x\in \mathcal{M}_{\infty}$, then $x.real, x.imag \in \mathcal{M}_{\infty}$ \ref{lem:M_inf_properties}. Thus we focus on $\cos(\alpha/3)$, which the real part $e^{\imath \frac{\pi}{3}}$ and a zero of \begin{equation*} f := 8 X^3 - 6 X - 1 \in \mathbb{Q}[X] \end{equation*} Suppose $f$ is reducible over $\mathbb{Q}$, then $f$ has a rational zero $a$, since $f$ is of degree $3$. According to the rational root theorem, a root rational root of $f$ is of the form $\pm \frac{p}{q}$ with $p$ a factor of the constant term and $q$ a factor of the leading coefficient. So the only possible rational zeros of $f$ are \begin{equation*} \{ \pm 1, \pm \frac{1}{2}, \pm \frac{1}{4}, \pm \frac{1}{8} \}. \end{equation*} One can check that none of these numbers are a zero of $f$. So $f$ is irreducible over $\mathbb{Q}$ and $\cos(\alpha/3) \notin \mathcal{M}_{\infty}$. Therefore \begin{equation*} \exp(\textbf{i} \alpha/3) \notin \mathcal{M}_{\infty} \end{equation*} So the angle $\pi / 3 = 60^{\circ}$ can't be trisected using a compass and straightedge.
